Is this a nuke or a hydrogen bomb, or are they the same thing?

A nuke can refer to either a fission(atom splitting) type nuclear weapon, or a fusion(atom fusing) type.

A thermonuclear bomb aka a hydrogen bomb, is a fusion reaction nuclear weapon. It works so that two hydrogen atoms fuse together under tremendous amounts of heat and pressure. When the two atoms fuse, they become a helium atom and release (yet again) tremendous amounts of energy. In a fusion type nuclear reaction, the tremendous amounts of heat and pressure required for the reaction to occur is supplied by a fission bomb. The first explosion triggers the second, they are 2 stage devices, though more stages can be added for a bigger bang.

Check this out for more.

The two bombs (fat man and little boy) dropped on Japan at the end of ww2 were fission type nuclear weapons. Fusion bombs were developed a few years later. On a side note, fusion of hydrogen is where the sun gets all it's energy from.
